subject.title: Text between tool calls leaks to messaging channels

question: Should normal external-channel direct and group/channel turns continue to auto-post bare assistant text by default, or should OpenClaw move those conversations to message-tool-only or final-only delivery with a migration/escape hatch?
rationale: The code and docs intentionally preserve automatic visible replies for compatibility, but that same default leaves internal/intermediate assistant text exposed in real messaging channels; automation cannot safely choose that product/security tradeoff.

options.title: Adopt safer external-channel defaults
options.body: Move external channel conversations toward message-tool-only or final-only delivery with an explicit migration or operator escape hatch, then close this after live channel proof.

options.title: Keep automatic defaults and add narrow guards
options.body: Preserve legacy bare-text reply behavior and only patch specific leak shapes such as reasoning/commentary payloads, accepting residual exposure risk.

options.title: Pause for a broader design item
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers split delivery defaults, progress previews, and cron announce semantics into separate sponsored work.

recommendation.title: Adopt safer external-channel defaults
recommendation.body: Move external channel conversations toward message-tool-only or final-only delivery with an explicit migration or operator escape hatch, then close this after live channel proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The current automatic visible-reply default and related docs/history point to this owner as the best available decision router for the compatibility tradeoff.
